Ridu 0.6.0 makes Go filters shorter to write and documents much cheaper to read and save. Filter helpers take field names as strings and compare them with ordinary Go values, so `query.Equal("owner", ctx.Actor.ID)` replaces a path, a wrapped value and an ignored error. The CMS still builds into one Go binary with its static admin embedded.

## Try Ridu

Install Go 1.25.13 or newer, Node.js 24 and Bun 1.4.0, then run:

```sh
bun create ridu@0.6.0 my-ridu-app
cd my-ridu-app
bun install
bun run dev
```

Choose SQLite for a local trial without a separate database service. See the [quickstart](https://riducms.com/docs/quickstart/) and [deployment guide](https://riducms.com/docs/production/).

## What changed

- `query.Equal`, `NotEqual`, `In`, `GreaterThan`, `GreaterThanEqual`, `LessThan`, `LessThanEqual`, `Contains` and `Like` take a field name such as `"seo.title"` and compare with strings, booleans, integers, floats and named types of those. A malformed name written in code panics; `query.ParsePath` still returns an error for names from input.
- For names and values known only at run time, the same helpers accept a `query.Path`, such as one from `ParsePath` or validated once when an access rule is built, and a `query.Value`, such as `query.Null()`, `query.DateTime(t)` or a value decoded from a request.
- `query.Exists("image", true)` matches documents that have a value for a field, and `false` matches documents without one.
- `query.Asc("title")` and `query.Desc("createdAt")` build sort terms. `query.NewSort` remains for directions chosen at run time.
- `query.DateTime(t)` converts a `time.Time` to the text a date-and-time field stores, so `query.GreaterThan("publishedAt", query.DateTime(time.Now()))` compares correctly with admin-saved values, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.
- `And` and `Or` share immutable condition nodes and merge nested conditions of the same kind. This reduces allocations when building filters; flattening still copies the child pointers into a new slice.
- The API reference shows generic constraints such as `query.FieldPath` with their type sets.
- Document values use a direct JSON codec with fewer intermediate objects for PostgreSQL and SQLite reads and writes of groups, arrays, blocks and rich text, and REST request bodies. The output remains compatible with `encoding/json`; differential tests and fuzzing check the encoding and decoding edge cases.
- Generated typed collection handles encode each document once instead of field by field.
- On 64-bit platforms, `store.Value` is 56 bytes instead of 72, reducing the memory occupied by each value.
- `Value.IsZero()` reports the zero `store.Value`, such as a missing map entry.

## Breaking changes and upgrading from 0.5.x

Run the new CLI's upgrade command from the project root, then review and commit the result:

```sh
bunx @riducms/cli@0.6.0 upgrade 0.6.0
```

Filters that wrap literal names and values, such as `query.Equal(query.Field("status"), query.String("published"))`, keep working and can be shortened to `query.Equal("status", "published")`. Two cases need a change:

- `query.In(path)` with no values cannot infer the value type. Pass an empty slice, as in `query.In(path, []string{}...)`.
- Integers beyond ±2^53 and NaN or infinite floats now panic in the helpers instead of losing precision. Compare such values as strings.

`store.ValueKind` is now a small integer type with a `String()` method. Comparisons with `store.ValueNull` and the other constants are unchanged. Replace `value.Kind() == ""` with `value.IsZero()`, and `string(value.Kind())` with `value.Kind().String()`: a plain conversion no longer produces the kind's name.

`And(And(a, b), c)` now produces one `And` with three conditions. Adapters and code that read `Expression.Node()` see the flatter tree; the matched documents are unchanged.

## Data and deployment compatibility

Update the Go framework, CLI, all `@riducms/*` packages and official plugins together to 0.6.0. Regenerate application contracts and rebuild the embedded admin before deploying.

The schema manifest, project-command protocol, REST/SDK wire contracts, plugin API markers and admin-plugin contracts retain their current formats. The JSON codec preserves the stored JSON representation. This release introduces no database migration format change or historical migration rewrite; review any migration plan caused by your own schema changes as usual.

PostgreSQL, SQLite and MongoDB retain their documented deployment boundaries. MongoDB qualification remains limited to generated starter/blank applications with MongoDB Community 8.2.9 on a writable, authenticated, TLS-verified three-member replica set on Linux x86-64.
